title: Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability
problemSolved: King’s does not yet have a sustained multidisciplinary team or consistent product practices for moving emerging student-experience needs from discovery and prototype into secure, supported institutional operation.
whatChanges: King’s establishes a four-post funded digital product core to deliver King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub through the three-year mobilisation and then transition into enduring Digital and IT business-as-usual capability. The four experienced core posts remain explicit and individually profiled: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, planned at approximately £61,000 for the eight-month November 2026 to June 2027 mobilisation period and £91,000 in each full year thereafter; 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, approximately £50,000 then £75,000 per full year; 1.0 FTE Product & Service Designer, approximately £50,000 then £75,000 per full year; and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer, approximately £42,000 then £63,000 per full year. This gives a four-post core staffing profile of approximately £203,000 in Year One and £304,000 in each of Years Two and Three, or approximately £811,000 across the three-year mobilisation in constant 2026 planning prices. In Years Two and Three, the core is augmented by one 1.0 FTE Junior Full-Stack Engineer on a paid sandwich-year placement, with a £35,000 annual employment envelope in each year. This is supervised additional capacity and a deliberate talent-pipeline test, not a replacement for the Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer or any other experienced core role. Total planned staffing therefore becomes approximately £203,000 in Year One and £339,000 in each of Years Two and Three, or approximately £881,000 across mobilisation. Digital and IT / HR must validate final grades, appointment points, placement route, start dates and future pay awards. The Product & Service Designer combines UX/UI, service design, prototyping and user research. Mark Peace is the Product Owner. Business-analysis capacity and DevOps/platform support are expected as small protected shared allocations rather than additional funded core posts. Product quality assurance sits with the QA Engineer, while specialist security, privacy, accessibility and architecture assurance are drawn from existing institutional functions when required. Solution architecture should be covered within the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer role if credible; otherwise a small additional shared allocation is required. Ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling is profiled throughout the three-year mobilisation at £90,000 per year, or £270,000 in total, while Digital and IT validates the exact commercial structure and whether reliable shared capacity can reduce actual spend. The current directly quantified 4.1.3 profile is therefore approximately £293,000 in Year One and £429,000 in each of Years Two and Three, or approximately £1.151m across the mobilisation, before valuing existing shared capacity. The wider Year One 4.1 baseline remains approximately £358,000 once the £50,000 Azure/environment/platform and £15,000 paid student co-design envelopes under 4.1.2 are included. From July 2029 the original four experienced posts are intended to transfer into recurrent Digital and IT establishment, with an indicative constant-price BAU staffing run-rate of approximately £304,000 per year. That recurrent run-rate is shown separately from the three-year mobilisation investment and is not double-counted. The remaining BAU decisions concern the recurrent funding route, final organisational arrangements and whether the agentic-tooling and junior-placement models also continue.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed that the 4.0 FTE funded product pod remains the Year One core. Broad digital-estate mapping and student-journey discovery require additional named and protected service-design and business-analysis capacity, with reliable user-research support. The planning assumption is to secure this through existing or seconded institutional capability where possible, without tying it to a particular organisational home or automatically enlarging the permanent pod. Specialist technical and assurance inputs remain time-bound and should be explicitly protected when needed.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Revised and clarified the Year One four-person product-core hypothesis. The funded posts are 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE product/UX/UI design capacity and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. QA may start later once code production is established. Digital and IT will confirm whether the senior engineering post can also fulfil solution architecture or whether architecture must be supplied separately.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed the mobilisation route: Education secures the investment through the strategic funding process and Digital and IT creates and recruits the technical roles through its workforce processes. The existing KAI team will not be transferred wholesale into the Hub capability, although reusable technical assets should be assessed deliberately, including Azure AI Foundry components.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Agentic software development should be incorporated into the Year One delivery model as an accelerator used by an experienced engineering team. Digital and IT discussed a possible dedicated instance at approximately £90,000; this is now included as a Year One planning allowance while the exact commercial structure and any opportunity to use shared capacity are validated.

Simplified the Year One capability model for Digital and IT validation. Mark Peace is the Product Owner. The funded design post is defined as a Product & Service Designer combining UX/UI, service design, prototyping and user research. Product quality assurance sits with the QA Engineer; specialist security, privacy, accessibility and architecture assurance remain institutional specialist inputs. Remove the previous separate delivery/agile, service-design, user-research and pooled-assurance FTE assumptions. Retain only small protected shared Business Analyst and DevOps/platform allocations, with conditional solution-architecture support if the senior engineer cannot carry it.

Removed the proposed sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer from the Year One mobilisation model. Costed the agentic software-development tooling into the Year One baseline at £90,000 as a planning allowance.

Replaced the £201,000 global staffing holding envelope with four role-level Year One estimates for November 2026 to June 2027. Planning assumptions are: Senior Backend & Integration Engineer at King’s Grade 8 midpoint, £61,000 including employer on-costs; Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer at Grade 7 midpoint, £50,000; Product & Service Designer at Grade 7 midpoint, £50,000; and QA Engineer at Grade 6 midpoint, £42,000. Total planned staffing is therefore approximately £203,000 and the overall Year One cash baseline approximately £358,000. Digital and IT / HR must validate final grades, appointment points and start dates.

Confirmed the four funded experienced posts as the core staffing assumption across the full three-year mobilisation rather than a Year One-only resource. The current constant-price core profile is approximately £203,000 in 2026/27 for the eight-month November-to-June mobilisation period, then approximately £304,000 in each of 2027/28 and 2028/29, giving approximately £811,000 across the three years.

Profiled ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling across all three mobilisation years at a £90,000 annual planning allowance, £270,000 total, subject to commercial validation and reduction where reliable shared institutional capacity is cheaper. Added one 1.0 FTE Junior Full-Stack Engineer sandwich-year placement in each of Years Two and Three at a £35,000 annual employment envelope. The placement is supervised augmentation to the four-post experienced core and tests productive junior contribution, learning value and a potential internal digital-talent pipeline; it does not replace the Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer or another core post.

Confirmed that the original four experienced digital-product posts are intended to transition into recurrent Digital and IT business-as-usual establishment from July 2029, rather than being subject to a later decision about whether the core capability survives. The current constant-price recurrent staffing run-rate is approximately £304,000 per year. This BAU liability is shown separately from the three-year mobilisation investment. The remaining end-of-mobilisation decisions concern the recurrent funding and organisational route and whether agentic tooling, the junior-placement model or any additional capacity should also continue.
